input: In 2015, the government needed a way to find undeclared Swiss accounts and shell-company wealth, and ordinary Income Tax Act penalties were too easy to litigate around. So Section 43 was written blunt on purpose: a flat penalty for non-disclosure, no need to prove evasion. That bluntness is also why the same rule now catches a forgotten $50 account exactly as hard as a real offshore fortune - the law was built to be a wide net, and a wide net does not sort by size.
